traces.intro: Seven times in John, Jesus says “I am” with a predicate — each one a claim about who he is. Behind them stands the absolute “I am” of John 8:58 (“Before Abraham was, I am”), echoing the name God gave Moses in Exodus 3:14.

items.label: I am the bread of life
items.note: Spoken the day after the feeding of the five thousand. As manna sustained Israel, he sustains all who come to him — and “shall never hunger.”

items.label: I am the light of the world
items.note: Said at the Feast of Tabernacles, when the great lamps lit the temple courts. In him there is no darkness at all.

items.label: I am the door
items.note: The sheepfold had one opening, guarded by the shepherd himself. Every approach to God goes through him.

items.label: I am the good shepherd
items.note: The shepherd who does not run from the wolf but lays down his life for the sheep — a direct prophecy of the cross.

items.label: I am the resurrection, and the life
items.note: Said at the tomb of Lazarus, moments before calling him out. Resurrection is not only an event; it is a person.

items.label: I am the way, and the truth, and the life
items.note: The most exclusive claim ever made: no one comes to the Father except through him.

items.label: I am the true vine
items.note: Israel was God's vine (Psalm 80, Isaiah 5). Jesus declares himself the true one — life flows only by abiding in him.

traces.title: The seven “I AM” sayings

traces.intro: John stacks titles for Jesus from the first chapter to the last — each one opening a different window onto who he is.

items.label: The Word
items.note: In the beginning was the Word — eternal, divine, the agent of creation itself.

items.label: The Lamb of God
items.note: John the Baptist's announcement: the Passover lamb to whom every sacrifice pointed, come to take away the sin of the world.

items.label: The Son of God
items.note: The Baptist's witness, confirmed by the Father's voice at the baptism.

items.label: The Messiah (the Christ)
items.note: Andrew's confession: the long-promised Anointed One has been found.

items.label: The King of Israel
items.note: Nathanael's confession under the fig tree — fulfilled openly at the triumphal entry (12:13).

items.label: The Son of Man
items.note: Jesus' own favorite title, drawn from Daniel 7:13 — the heavenly figure given everlasting dominion.

items.label: The Saviour of the world
items.note: The Samaritans' confession: salvation is not for one nation only.

items.label: The Holy One of God
items.note: Peter's confession when many disciples walked away — “Lord, to whom shall we go?”

items.label: Sanctified and sent by the Father
items.note: Consecrated for his mission — the Sent One, in John's constant language.

items.label: My Lord and my God
items.note: Thomas's climax: the Gospel's highest confession, and Jesus blesses all who believe without seeing.

traces.title: Titles of Christ in John

traces.intro: John keeps pausing the narrative to say “that the scripture might be fulfilled.” Here are the promise-and-fulfillment pairs, mostly clustered around the cross.

items.label: They part my garments — Psalm 22:18
items.note: The soldiers divide his clothes and cast lots for his tunic, exactly as the psalm described a thousand years earlier.

items.label: Vinegar to drink — Psalm 69:21
items.note: “I thirst” — spoken, John says, so that even this detail of the psalm would be fulfilled.

items.label: Not a bone broken — Exodus 12:46; Psalm 34:20
items.note: The Passover lamb's bones were not to be broken. Neither were his.

items.label: They shall look on him whom they pierced — Zechariah 12:10
items.note: The spear, the blood and water — Zechariah's pierced one, mourned like an only son.

items.label: Thy king cometh on a colt — Zechariah 9:9
items.note: The triumphal entry rides straight out of Zechariah's prophecy.

items.label: Zeal for thy house — Psalm 69:9
items.note: The disciples remembered this psalm as Jesus drove the traders from the temple.

items.label: Betrayed by a friend — Psalm 41:9
items.note: “He that eateth my bread lifted up his heel against me” — Judas at the table.

items.label: Hated without a cause — Psalm 35:19; 69:4
items.note: The world's hatred of Jesus fulfills the psalms of the righteous sufferer.

items.label: Who hath believed our report? — Isaiah 53:1
items.note: Isaiah's suffering-servant chapter explains Israel's unbelief — and identifies Jesus as the servant.

traces.title: Prophecies fulfilled

traces.intro: John calls Jesus' miracles “signs” — each one points past itself to who he is. John 20:31 says they were written “that ye may believe.”

items.label: Water into wine at Cana
items.note: The first sign: the master of the feast tastes the new wine of the kingdom.

items.label: Healing the nobleman's son
items.note: Healed from a distance by a word — faith without sight, honored.

items.label: The paralytic at Bethesda
items.note: Thirty-eight years waiting by the pool; one word — “Arise” — and he walks.

items.label: Feeding the five thousand
items.note: The only miracle in all four Gospels — the new manna, pointing to the Bread of Life.

items.label: Walking on the water
items.note: “It is I” — literally “I am” — and the wind ceases.

items.label: Healing the man born blind
items.note: Mud, Siloam, and sight — the Light of the World giving light to dark eyes.

items.label: Raising Lazarus
items.note: Four days dead, and the Resurrection calls him out — the sign that sealed Jesus' own death sentence.

traces.title: The seven signs

traces.intro: If you read nothing else: the twelve verses that carry the whole Gospel, from eternity past to the reason it was written.

items.label: For God so loved the world
The way, the truth, the life
